title: Perp-Neg: negatives that do not fight the prompt
hook: Plain cfg cancels whatever your two prompts share. Perp-Neg removes only the part of the negative at right angles to the positive, for one more prediction per step.

verified.claim: perp_neg computes nocond + cfg times (pos minus neg_scale times perp), with perp the negative's part at right angles to the positive.
The lab's port equals the real perp_neg on test tensors.
verified.ref: Our comparison on a CPU, v0.43.0

verified.claim: The formula matches Eq. 8 of the paper, with its negative weight equal to cfg times neg_scale.
The dot product in the source sums over the whole tensor, batch included.
The guider predicts positive, negative and empty together, and drops the negative at neg_scale 0, and the empty as well at cfg 1.
Our render's settings and difference figure are stored from one seed.

unchecked: Our one render uses an ordinary negative that doesn't overlap the prompt. It doesn't test the overlap case Perp-Neg is for. We list that render as wanted.
That the batch-wide dot product matters in practice is our inference. The lab only shows that the sum isn't per image.
